note: The first couple; Eve is formed from Adam and named by him "mother of all living".
Firstborn son of Adam and Eve.
Eve names Cain, saying she has gotten a man with the LORD.
Second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep.
Second son of Eve.
Born in Adam's likeness after Abel's death; the line of promise continues through him.
Eve names him Seth, "appointed", in place of Abel.
Cain murders his brother out of jealousy over God's regard for Abel's offering.
descendant (generations omitted): Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel and Jared stand between them; Enoch is "the seventh from Adam" (Jude 1:14).
Enoch begets Methuselah at sixty-five, after which he "walked with God".
descendant (generations omitted): Methuselah is Noah's grandfather through Lamech.
Son of Noah; blessed by his father, and ancestor of Abraham.
Son of Noah; his act of seeing his father's nakedness leads to the curse on Canaan.
Son of Noah; blessed with enlargement.
descendant (generations omitted): the Shem genealogy runs nine generations to Terah.
Terah is the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran.
Abraham says Sarah is his father's daughter but not his mother's, making Terah her father.
descendant (generations omitted): Lot is Terah's grandson through Haran.
Abram marries Sarai, his half-sister; God renames her Sarah and promises her a son.
Sarai gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram "to be his wife" as a surrogate.
Abram's firstborn son, by Hagar; God promises to make him a great nation.
The angel of the LORD tells Hagar to name her son Ishmael, "God hears".
The son of promise, born when Abraham was a hundred years old.
Sarah bears Isaac in old age and names him for her laughter.
Rivalry between mistress and servant leads to Hagar's flight and later expulsion.
Uncle and nephew; they part to avoid strife, and Abram later rescues Lot from captivity.
The priest-king of Salem blesses Abram, who gives him a tenth of the spoil.
The two half-brothers together bury Abraham at Machpelah.
Isaac takes Rebekah into Sarah's tent and loves her.
Elder twin son of Isaac, favoured by his father.
Younger twin son of Isaac, who receives the blessing.
Elder twin, born red and hairy.
Younger twin, loved by Rebekah, who helps him obtain the blessing.
Laban is Rebekah's brother and helps arrange her marriage to Isaac.
Jacob takes Esau's birthright and blessing; Esau plans to kill him, but they are reconciled years later.
Laban's elder daughter.
Laban's younger daughter.
Uncle and father-in-law who deceives Jacob over his wages and wives; they part under a boundary covenant.
Laban substitutes Leah for Rachel on the wedding night.
Jacob serves fourteen years for Rachel, whom he loves more than Leah.
Sisters and co-wives in rivalry over Jacob's love and over children.
Jacob's firstborn, by Leah.
Leah names him Reuben, "see, a son".
Third son of Jacob by Leah; ancestor of the priestly tribe.
Leah hopes her husband will now be "joined" to her.
Fourth son of Jacob; receives the blessing of the sceptre.
Leah says, "Now will I praise the LORD".
Rachel's firstborn, loved by Jacob more than his other sons.
Born after long barrenness; Rachel asks for another son.
Youngest son of Jacob; Jacob renames him from Ben-oni to Benjamin.
Rachel dies giving birth to him near Bethlehem.
Reuben tries to save Joseph from his brothers, meaning to return him to their father.
Judah proposes selling Joseph; years later he offers himself in Benjamin's place, leading to reconciliation.
Full brothers through Rachel; Joseph weeps over Benjamin on revealing himself.
Tamar is Judah's daughter-in-law; deceived by her, he admits "she hath been more righteous than I" and she bears him twins.
descendant (generations omitted): through Perez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon and Salmon.
descendant (generations omitted): Tamar is mother of Perez, ancestor of Boaz.
descendant (generations omitted): Saul is from the tribe of Benjamin.
descendant (generations omitted): Paul calls himself "of the tribe of Benjamin".
descendant (generations omitted): Mordecai is "a Benjamite".
descendant (generations omitted): Amram is Levi's grandson through Kohath.
Amram marries Jochebed, his father's sister.
Father of Moses.
Father of Aaron.
Father of Miriam.
She hides the infant Moses and is hired to nurse him for Pharaoh's daughter.
Mother of Aaron.
Mother of Miriam.
Zipporah is one of the seven daughters of the priest of Midian.
Moses marries Zipporah in Midian; she circumcises their son on the road to Egypt.
Moses' father-in-law advises him to appoint judges to share the burden.
Aaron acts as spokesman for his brother before Pharaoh.
Micah names Moses, Aaron and Miriam as the leaders God sent before Israel.
Miriam and Aaron together challenge Moses' unique authority and Miriam is struck with leprosy.
Moses repeatedly demands that Pharaoh let Israel go; Pharaoh refuses until the final plague.
Aaron's rod becomes a serpent before Pharaoh and swallows the magicians' rods.
Joshua serves as Moses' minister from his youth.
Moses lays hands on Joshua, who leads Israel into Canaan.
Third son of Aaron and Elisheba.
Aaron's garments are put on Eleazar on Mount Hor before Aaron dies.
Phinehas is Eleazar's son.
Phinehas succeeds his father as priest in the line of high priests.
Priest and leader together distribute the land of Canaan.
Korah leads a revolt against Moses and Aaron and is swallowed by the earth.
Korah, a Levite, seeks the priesthood reserved for Aaron.
Phinehas goes with the army against Midian, in which campaign Balaam is killed for his counsel that led Israel astray.
The two faithful spies urge Israel to trust God; both later enter the land.
Caleb quiets the people before Moses and is promised Hebron.
Othniel, son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz, captures Debir and marries Caleb's daughter Achsah.
Rahab hides Joshua's spies; Joshua spares her and her family at Jericho.
Matthew's genealogy names Rahab as the mother of Boaz by Salmon; many read this as a remote ancestor, since the span from the conquest to Boaz seems longer than one generation.
After the death of Joshua's generation, Othniel is the first judge raised up.
Next judge in the narrative after Othniel.
After Ehud's death (and Shamgar's brief deliverance), Deborah judges Israel.
The next judge after Deborah's forty years of rest.
Later judge in the narrative; Abimelech, Tola and Jair intervene.
Later judge; Ibzan, Elon and Abdon intervene.
Deborah summons Barak to fight Sisera and goes with him; they sing the victory song together.
Jael kills Sisera and shows his body to the pursuing Barak.
Deborah foretells that a woman will defeat Sisera and praises Jael in her song.
Samson loves Delilah; bribed by the Philistine lords, she discovers the secret of his strength.
Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law; Ruth vows to stay with Naomi, who later guides her toward Boaz.
Boaz is a kinsman of Naomi's husband Elimelech and redeems the family land.
Boaz acts as kinsman-redeemer and marries Ruth the Moabite.
Son of Boaz and Ruth.
The LORD gives Ruth conception and she bears Obed.
Naomi becomes Obed's nurse; the women say "there is a son born to Naomi".
Obed is the father of Jesse.
David is the youngest of Jesse's sons, chosen and anointed by Samuel.
Hannah prays for a son and dedicates him to the LORD.
Eli first mistakes Hannah's prayer for drunkenness, then blesses her.
Samuel ministers before the LORD under Eli, who teaches him to answer God's call.
Eli judged Israel forty years; Samuel judges Israel all his life after him.
descendant (generations omitted): the man of God addresses Eli as belonging to the house God chose from all the tribes for priesthood, i.e. Aaron's line.
Samuel anoints Saul as the first king.
Samuel rebukes Saul for unauthorized sacrifice and for sparing Agag, announcing the kingdom will be taken from him.
Samuel anoints David and shelters him at Ramah when he flees Saul.
Jonathan is Saul's son.
Michal is Saul's younger daughter.
Saul's jealousy drives him to hunt David, who twice spares his life.
After Saul's death David is anointed king, first over Judah, then over all Israel.
Jonathan loves David as his own soul and makes a covenant with him.
Michal loves David and saves his life; later she despises him for dancing before the ark.
Abigail, widow of Nabal, becomes David's wife after her wise intervention.
David takes Bathsheba after arranging Uriah's death; she bears Solomon.
Bathsheba is the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
David has Uriah, one of his loyal soldiers, placed where he will be killed.
Third son of David, by Maacah.
Absalom revolts and drives his father from Jerusalem; David mourns his death.
Joab first brings Absalom home, then kills him against David's order.
Joab is commander of David's army and carries out his orders, including the death of Uriah.
On David's charge Solomon has Joab executed for past bloodshed and his support of Adonijah.
Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb exposes David's sin: "Thou art the man."
Nathan delivers the oracle of the everlasting Davidic dynasty.
Gad advises David while in the wilderness and is later remembered as a recorder of his acts.
After David's census Gad brings God's choice of three punishments and tells him to build an altar on Araunah's threshing floor.
Nathan and Bathsheba together secure Solomon's succession against Adonijah.
Nathan names the infant Solomon Jedidiah and later anoints him king.
Son of David and Bathsheba.
Bathsheba bears Solomon; as queen mother she sits at his right hand.
Solomon is anointed and sits on the throne of David his father.
The queen tests Solomon with hard questions and exchanges lavish gifts with him.
Son of Solomon by Naamah the Ammonitess.
Rehoboam reigns in Solomon's place.
Solomon's labour officer rebels; Solomon seeks to kill him and he flees to Egypt.
The kingdom divides; there is war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
Ahab marries the Sidonian princess Jezebel, who stirs him up to evil.
Elijah calls Ahab the troubler of Israel and condemns him over Naboth's vineyard.
Jezebel vows to kill Elijah after Carmel; Elijah prophesies her death at Jezreel.
Elijah casts his mantle on Elisha, who leaves his oxen to serve him.
Elisha receives a double portion of Elijah's spirit and his mantle.
Elijah is commissioned to anoint Jehu king over Israel.
Elisha sends a son of the prophets to anoint Jehu and charge him to destroy Ahab's house.
Elisha tells the Syrian commander to wash seven times in the Jordan, and he is healed.
Micaiah alone foretells Ahab's defeat and is imprisoned for it.
Jehoshaphat insists on hearing a prophet of the LORD, and Micaiah is summoned.
Judah and Israel ally by marriage and fight together at Ramoth-gilead.
Athaliah is "the daughter of Ahab" and granddaughter of Omri; whether Jezebel was her mother is not stated.
Jehu has Jezebel thrown from a window at Jezreel.
Jehu wipes out the house of Ahab as Elijah foretold.
descendant (generations omitted): Joash is Athaliah's grandson through Ahaziah.
Athaliah tries to destroy the royal seed; the infant Joash is hidden and later crowned, and she is killed.
descendant (generations omitted): through Abijam and Asa.
descendant (generations omitted): through Jehoram and Ahaziah.
descendant (generations omitted): through Amaziah; Uzziah is also called Azariah.
descendant (generations omitted): through Jotham and Ahaz.
Manasseh is Hezekiah's son.
Manasseh reigns in his father's place at age twelve.
descendant (generations omitted): through Amon.
Zedekiah (Mattaniah) is a son of Josiah, set on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar.
descendant (generations omitted): through Jeconiah and Shealtiel (or Pedaiah, per 1 Chr 3:19).
descendant (generations omitted): Zephaniah traces his line to "Hizkiah", commonly but not certainly identified with King Hezekiah.
Isaiah assures Hezekiah that Jerusalem will be delivered from Assyria.
Isaiah announces Hezekiah's death (later reversed) and rebukes his display of treasures to Babylon.
Micah prophesies Zion's ploughing; Hezekiah fears the LORD and the disaster is averted.
Isaiah delivers God's taunt against the Assyrian king's pride.
Sennacherib invades Judah and besieges Jerusalem; his army is struck down.
Tradition (e.g. *Ascension of Isaiah*) says Manasseh had Isaiah sawn in two; Scripture says only that Manasseh shed much innocent blood and Hebrews mentions martyrs "sawn asunder".
The prophetess confirms the warnings of the rediscovered law book and promises Josiah peace in his lifetime.
Zephaniah prophesies in the days of Josiah, during the period of his reform.
Jeremiah's ministry begins under Josiah; he laments the king's death and holds him up as just.
Jeremiah tells Zedekiah privately to surrender to Babylon; the king is too afraid to obey.
Baruch writes Jeremiah's words from his dictation and reads them publicly.
Nebuchadnezzar orders that Jeremiah be well treated after Jerusalem falls.
Nebuchadnezzar installs Zedekiah, then blinds him and takes him to Babylon after his rebellion.
Daniel interprets the king's dreams and urges him to break off his sins by righteousness.
Fellow Judean exiles trained in Babylon; Daniel asks them to pray with him and secures their appointment.
Fellow exiles and companions in prayer.
Fellow exiles and companions in prayer.
They refuse together to worship the golden image and are delivered from the furnace.
Companions in the furnace.
Their shared answer to the king.
The king throws the three into the furnace, then blesses their God and promotes them.
Daniel continues and prospers into the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
Cyrus' decree permits the return under which Zerubbabel leads the rebuilding.
Mordecai raises his orphaned cousin Esther and urges her to act "for such a time as this".
Governor and high priest lead the rebuilding of the altar and temple together.
Haggai urges Zerubbabel to build and calls him God's signet ring.
Haggai's oracles are addressed to Joshua as well as Zerubbabel.
Zechariah sees Joshua cleansed and crowned as a sign of the coming Branch.
"Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit" is spoken to Zerubbabel.
The two prophets together stir up the rebuilding of the temple.
Ezra reads the law while Nehemiah is governor; both lead the wall dedication.
descendant (generations omitted): Ezra's priestly genealogy runs back to "Aaron the chief priest".
descendant (generations omitted): Ezra descends from Phinehas son of Eleazar.
descendant (generations omitted): Joshua is the son of Josedech (Jehozadak), the last in the Aaronic high-priestly line carried into exile.
descendant (generations omitted): Matthew's line runs from Zerubbabel through Abiud to Jacob, father of Joseph.
John comes "in the spirit and power of Elias"; Jesus identifies him as the Elijah who was to come.
Joseph is betrothed to Mary and, after the angel's message, takes her as his wife.
Legal father of Jesus; Luke notes Jesus was "as was supposed" the son of Joseph.
Mary conceives by the Holy Spirit and bears Jesus at Bethlehem.
Descendant: Jesus is called the son of David, heir to his throne.
Descendant: Matthew opens with Jesus as son of Abraham; Paul calls Christ the promised "seed".
Descendant: Luke traces Jesus' genealogy back to Adam, "the son of God".
A righteous, childless priestly couple in old age.
Gabriel announces John's birth; Zechariah confirms the name in writing.
Elizabeth conceives in old age and insists the child be named John.
descendant (generations omitted): Elizabeth is "of the daughters of Aaron".
descendant (generations omitted): Zechariah serves in the priestly course of Abijah.
Relatives (KJV "cousin"); Mary visits Elizabeth, whose child leaps at her greeting.
Simeon takes the infant Jesus in his arms and blesses God for seeing his salvation.
Simeon tells Mary that a sword will pierce her own soul.
The aged prophetess gives thanks and speaks of the child to all who looked for redemption.
Herod tries to kill the newborn king and slaughters the children of Bethlehem.
Antipas is a son of Herod the Great (stated by Josephus; the Gospels call him "Herod the tetrarch").
On Herod's death his kingdom is divided; Antipas becomes tetrarch of Galilee and Perea.
descendant (generations omitted): Agrippa I is Herod the Great's grandson through Aristobulus (Josephus).
Agrippa II is the son of Agrippa I (Josephus); Bernice is his sister.
John baptizes Jesus and points to him as the Lamb of God; they are kinsmen through their mothers.
Andrew is a disciple of John before following Jesus.
John rebukes Herod for taking his brother's wife Herodias and is imprisoned.
Herod respects John yet beheads him at Herodias' daughter's request.
Jesus calls Herod "that fox" and later stays silent before him.
Previously at enmity, Pilate and Herod become friends the day of Jesus' trial.
Jesus calls Simon, renames him Peter, and after the resurrection commissions him to feed his sheep.
Called with his brother as fishers of men.
Called from the boats; part of the inner circle, nicknamed a son of thunder.
Called with his brother James; traditionally identified as the disciple whom Jesus loved.
Jesus finds Philip and tells him "Follow me".
One of the Twelve; if he is Nathanael, Jesus calls him an Israelite without guile.
Thomas doubts the resurrection and then confesses "My Lord and my God".
Jesus calls the tax collector from the receipt of custom.
Named among the Twelve.
Named among the Twelve; probably the "Judas not Iscariot" who questions Jesus at the supper.
Named among the Twelve.
Chosen as one of the Twelve and keeper of the common purse.
Judas betrays Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
Judas bargains with the chief priests gathered at Caiaphas' palace.
Matthias is chosen by lot to take Judas' place among the Twelve.
Brothers; Andrew brings Simon to Jesus.
Brothers, sons of Zebedee; together they ask for the seats of honour.
Partners at the tomb, at the healing at the temple gate, and on the mission to Samaria.
Both from Bethsaida; together they bring the Greeks' request to Jesus.
Philip brings Nathanael to Jesus; Nathanael is traditionally identified with Bartholomew, who is paired with Philip in the lists.
Delivered from seven devils, she supports Jesus' ministry and is the first to see the risen Lord.
She reports the empty tomb to Peter and the beloved disciple.
Mary sits at Jesus' feet to hear his word and later anoints him.
Martha hosts Jesus and confesses him as the Christ.
Jesus loves Lazarus and raises him from the dead.
Sisters of Bethany.
Martha and Mary are Lazarus' sisters.
Brother and sister of Bethany.
The Pharisee comes by night to learn and later defends Jesus' right to a hearing.
Together they bury Jesus' body with spices.
A secret disciple and council member who asks Pilate for the body and lays it in his own tomb.
Pilate grants Joseph the body of Jesus.
The chief tax collector receives Jesus joyfully and repays fourfold.
Pilate finds no fault in Jesus yet hands him over to be crucified.
Caiaphas counsels that one man should die for the people and presides at Jesus' hearing.
Annas is the father-in-law of Caiaphas.
Jesus is first taken to Annas for questioning.
The high-priestly family threatens Peter and John and forbids them to preach.
Annas sits in the council that questions Peter and John.
From the cross Jesus entrusts his mother to the beloved disciple.
Named among Jesus' brothers. Protestants usually read this as Mary's son; Orthodox tradition as a son of Joseph by an earlier marriage; Catholic tradition as a cousin.
Named among Jesus' brothers (Juda/Judas); the same debate over "brothers" applies.
Jude calls himself "brother of James".
At first unbelieving, James sees the risen Jesus and becomes a leader of the church.
Mary prays with the apostles in the upper room before Pentecost.
The risen Christ appears to Saul and Paul says he received his gospel by revelation of Jesus Christ.
Paul visits Peter in Jerusalem; they agree on missions to circumcised and uncircumcised. Paul later opposes Peter at Antioch (Gal 2:11-14), and 2 Peter calls Paul "our beloved brother".
Peter preaches in Cornelius' house and the Spirit falls on the Gentiles.
Peter raises Dorcas (Tabitha) at Joppa.
Peter goes to Mark's mother's house and calls him "Marcus my son"; tradition makes Mark Peter's interpreter.
Peter writes "by Silvanus, a faithful brother", usually identified with Silas.
Both are pillars of the Jerusalem church and speak at the council.
Peter and John follow up Philip's mission in Samaria.
James extends the right hand of fellowship and advises Paul in Jerusalem.
Herod kills James the brother of John with the sword.
Herod imprisons Peter, who is freed by an angel.
Saul guards the clothes of those stoning Stephen and consents to his death.
Both are among the seven chosen to serve tables.
The apostles appoint the seven, including Stephen, and lay hands on them.
Paul was "brought up at the feet of Gamaliel".
Gamaliel counsels the council to leave the apostles alone lest they fight against God.
Philip explains Isaiah 53 and baptizes the Ethiopian official.
Paul stays in Philip's house at Caesarea.
Agabus binds himself with Paul's girdle to foretell his arrest in Jerusalem.
Agabus predicts a famine; Barnabas and Saul carry the relief to Judea.
Barnabas vouches for the new convert and later brings him to Antioch.
Partners on the first missionary journey; they part after a sharp disagreement over Mark.
Barnabas insists on taking Mark again and sails with him to Cyprus.
Mark is "sister's son to Barnabas" (KJV); modern versions say cousin.
Mark leaves the first journey, but later Paul calls him "profitable to me for the ministry".
Silas is sent with Paul and Barnabas to carry the council's letter.
Paul's companion on the second journey; imprisoned with him at Philippi.
Paul takes Timothy on mission and calls him his own son in the faith.
Silas and Timothy work together in Macedonia and Corinth.
An uncircumcised Greek convert whom Paul calls his own son and leaves in Crete.
Both serve as Paul's envoys to Corinth; Paul calls Titus "my partner and fellowhelper".
The beloved physician, a fellow labourer who stays with Paul to the end; the "we" passages of Acts are traditionally his.
Both send greetings with Paul as fellow workers.
The seller of purple opens her heart and home to Paul at Philippi.
Paul and Silas visit Lydia's house after their release.
A Jewish couple, tentmakers expelled from Rome under Claudius.
Paul works and lodges with them at Corinth; they risked their necks for him.
Fellow tentmaker who sails with Paul to Ephesus.
Priscilla and Aquila expound the way of God more perfectly to Apollos.
With Priscilla he instructs Apollos.
Paul planted, Apollos watered; Paul urges him to visit Corinth.
Paul commends Phoebe, a servant (deacon) of the church at Cenchreae and his patron.
Paul's kinsman and fellow prisoner, "of note among the apostles", in Christ before Paul.
Paul's kinswoman and fellow prisoner, "of note among the apostles" (sense debated).
Greeted together; often taken as a married missionary couple, though the text does not say so.
Paul calls Onesimus his son begotten in his bonds and sends him back as a brother.
Paul addresses Philemon as "dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer".
Onesimus is Philemon's slave; Paul asks him to receive Onesimus as a beloved brother.
Paul reasons with Felix of righteousness, temperance and judgment to come; Felix trembles but hopes for a bribe.
Paul appeals to Caesar before Festus and answers his charge of madness.
Paul makes his defence before Agrippa, who says "almost thou persuadest me".
Porcius Festus succeeds Felix as procurator of Judea.
Festus consults Agrippa about Paul's case.
Timothy is named as co-sender of several letters.
Both speak at the Jerusalem council; at Antioch Barnabas follows Peter's withdrawal from Gentile tables.
Corinthian factions claim Paul, Apollos and Cephas; Paul says all are servants belonging to the church.
